Title: Transformer Architecture
Summary: The image illustrates the architecture of a Transformer model, featuring two main components: the encoder and decoder. The encoder consists of multiple layers (N×) that include 'Add & Norm', 'Feed Forward', and 'Multi-Head Attention' blocks. The decoder mirrors this structure but includes a 'Masked Multi-Head Attention' block to prevent attending to future tokens. Positional encoding is applied to both input and output embeddings to retain the order of the sequence. The output probabilities are generated through a linear layer followed by a softmax function.

Title: Table 3: Variations on the Transformer architecture
Summary: Table 3 presents variations on the Transformer architecture, focusing on metrics for the English-to-German translation development set, newsets2013. The base model has parameters N=6, d_model=512, d_ff=2048, h=8, d_k=64, d_v=64, P_drop=0.1, and train steps=100K, yielding a perplexity (PPL) of 5.29 and a BLEU score of 28.4 with 65 million parameters. Variation (A) shows configurations with attention heads and dimensions, achieving PPL values of 5.00, 4.91, and 5.01 for different setups, with BLEU scores ranging from 25.4 to 25.8. Variation (B) indicates that reducing attention key size d_k to 16 results in a PPL of 5.19 and a BLEU score of 25.3. Variation (C) explores larger models with N=2, 4, and 8, yielding PPL values from 4.88 to 6.11 and BLEU scores from 23.7 to 26.0. Variation (D) assesses dropout rates of 0.0 and 0.2, with PPL values of 5.77 and 4.67, respectively. Variation (E) examines positional embeddings, achieving a PPL of 4.92 and a BLEU score of 25.7. The overall trend indicates that larger models and appropriate dropout rates improve performance, while reducing attention heads may negatively impact quality.
